title: Urology and Continence Supply Program patient account: payments, adjustments, refunds and payment plans
content:
The customer's balance on a Urology and Continence Supply Program is the running total of its patient-balance postings. Remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds add to it. Payments and balance adjustments reduce it. A balance below zero is a credit balance.

## 1. Applying payments

A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid posting first. *This clause is no longer in force for counting the waived amount of a hardship waiver under the current basis for such a waiver. For every other purpose it remains in force.*

## 2. Balance adjustments

2.1 A balance adjustment is posted only for one of the reasons below. Each is posted against the one posting it adjusts and never for more than that posting's unpaid remainder. *That posting-and-remainder clause is no longer in force for a hardship waiver handled under the current basis for such a waiver. Every other balance adjustment remains under it.*

| Reason | What it covers |
|---|---|
| Return credit | An accepted self-pay return, for the price paid for the returned units less the tier's restocking fee percent. *This definition is no longer in force as the only kind of return credit: a return credit on non-covered straight-tip catheter units of a Continence Commercial HMO Program is settled under the current basis for such a credit. Every self-pay return credit remains under this definition.* |
| Secondary-payer payment | The amount a secondary payer paid against a remittance's patient responsibility. |
| Hardship waiver | See section 3. |
| Small-balance write-off | See section 4. |
| Billing correction | A posting made in error, or a timely-filing write-off. |

## 3. Hardship waiver

A hardship waiver is granted only on tiers where a hardship waiver is available. It is granted only for postings named on a hardship application whose request status is approved. *That named-postings clause is no longer in force for a hardship waiver handled under the current basis for such a waiver. Every balance adjustment other than such a hardship waiver remains under it.* It is granted only after Larkfield's financial counseling team confirms household income at or below the tier's hardship income ceiling, as a percent of the HHS poverty guideline. A hardship waiver is never granted routinely, never advertised and never granted on the customer's statement alone. The approval status of the application on file is the evidence.

## 4. Small-balance write-off

A small-balance write-off is made only when the whole remaining balance of the program is greater than 0.00 USD and no more than the tier's small-balance ceiling. On tiers whose ceiling is 0.00 USD, no write-off is made and the balance is statemented.

| Hypothetical remaining balance on a 4.99 USD tier | Write-off? |
|---|---|
| 0.00 USD | no: the balance is not greater than 0.00 |
| 4.99 USD | yes |
| 5.00 USD | no: statemented |

## 5. Credit balances

A credit balance is refunded to the original payment method no later than the tier's credit refund limit, in calendar days after the posting date of the entry that created it, unless the customer asks in writing to keep it on account. A refund never exceeds the credit.

## 6. Payment plans

A payment plan is offered only on tiers whose longest plan term is greater than 0, and only for a balance of at least the tier's smallest plan balance. It runs in no more than the tier's longest plan term in monthly installments, each of at least the tier's smallest monthly installment. *That term-and-installment clause is no longer in force for a payment plan on a Continence Commercial HMO Program that the current basis for such a plan settles. Every other payment plan remains under it.* A plan is created as a payment plan request that the customer accepts. While an approved plan's installments are current, the balance it covers is left out of the past-due test.
